rationale:
The greedy-selected portfolio is the best and most robust artifact of the run: valid primary 0.6056 (GAUC 0.6729, nDCG@5 0.5383), +0.0040 vs the 0.6016 FM baseline and +0.0016 vs the best single model (0.6040), which is above the 0.0012 noise floor. Two independent ensemble_search runs reproduced it (0.6054 then 0.6056), so the number is not a lucky draw.

Why the ensemble rather than the best single entry: the final selection is 10 members spanning three structurally different objectives -- pairwise BPR (0.36 total weight), pointwise BCE (0.28) and the DIN target-attention head over user history (0.38) -- and averaging across objectives and seeds is exactly the variance reduction that transfers when the hidden test is a LATER time window than validation. The best single entry (0.6040) is one seed of one family and its edge over its own family mean (0.6026) is within seed sigma, i.e. partly selection noise on validation; the ensemble does not depend on that draw.

Honest read of the unbiased log: the ensemble scores 0.3713 on the randomised-exposure log versus ~0.372 for the strongest singles. That is flat, not up -- the ensemble gain does NOT clearly replicate off-policy, so I am reporting it as a modest, partly logging-policy-aligned improvement rather than a large one. I still prefer it because flat-unbiased-plus-up-validation from seed/objective averaging is a variance story, not an overfitting story: nothing here was selected against the unbiased log, and no member was chosen for a validation quirk. The one direction that moved the unbiased log strongly upward (fm_aux, per-video engagement priors, unbiased 0.3772, the run's best) was validation-negative at 0.5988 and earned zero ensemble weight, and I did not submit it -- it is recorded as a finding, since chasing it would have meant optimising a metric the task is not scored on.

rationale: Smoke test before search. CIN's Hadamard-against-X0 then 1x1-conv compression then sum-pooling is a vector-wise inductive bias distinct from DeepFM's bit-wise MLP, with degree growing exactly one per layer. Confirming finite loss and shape correctness cheaply (8 epochs) is far cheaper than discovering a bug inside a tune sweep.
